records.c: object type 15, the level's end boss: a machine five sprites across and four rows down (sprites $D4 to $E7), drawn by sprites 3 to 7 used again for each row by interrupts of its own. While it is on, the level runs its own sprites ($03ED) and the screen stops scrolling. It slides in from the right edge, moves left and right at random speeds, and from its third move on ends each move by stamping down and shaking the screen. It has 255 energy, and each weapon hit takes that weapon's damage from the table at $0720. Destroyed, it flashes for 30 frames, breaks into nine pieces of debris (type 13) and gives 10,000 points
its first frame waits, the object left new, until the hero is on the ground ($29 and $26 zero) and the fine scroll is at rest ($17 = 4, $16 = 3)

takes the screen over: the level runs its own sprites ($03ED); the scroll stops, its decision at $084D pointed at the RTS at $085D and both scroll stages ($0718, $071A) at the interrupt's exit; its raster routine $7083 replaces the multiplexer ($071E), and $6FED and $6D12 go into the level's frame vectors at $0862 and $0865. 255 energy ($BEEF), a first move left at 4 pixels a frame for 47 frames
places the five columns at X $64, $79, $8E, $A3 and $B8 with the high bit set (356 to 440, past the right edge), and the four rows at their starting Y from $728B
removes every object but the boss itself
writes the shown screen's page plus 3 ($0205) into the five STAs of the raster routine, so it sets the sprite pointers at the end of that screen

the boss's routine each frame after the first: puts back the top lines lent at the last row ($71FF), then, unless destroyed, tests for the hero's shots ($6EE0) and for touching him ($6FAE); moves it ($6D80) and, while it runs its sprites, sets the first row up for the next frame ($6D12)

finds the first row whose Y is on the play area ($33 to $D5) and puts it in $0223. A row above it that reaches into the top of the screen is shown first ($0224), its Y in sprites 3 to 7, with the first interrupt a line above the next row ($03EB); a top row on the screen sets the sprites to it at once. When the next row's line is a bad one it lends that row's top lines ($7155)
the top row is on the screen: sprites 3 to 7 take its Y
moves the boss. While $BEEE counts down the screen shakes, the fine scroll ($17) random each frame; otherwise it is 4. Then by state: 0 sideways, 1 stamping down, 2 rising, 3 destroyed

state 0, moving sideways: by the speed in $BEEB, to the right while $BEEA is set until the left column's X reaches 240, to the left until it is under 24 with no high bit; a carry or borrow flips that column's high bit ($726E)
rows 1 to 3 take row 0's X and high bits

the move's time ($BEE9) runs out: a new time of 0 to 127 frames and speed of about 1 to 4, the direction turned round; $BEEC counts the first two moves, and every move after them ends in a stamp (state 1)
state 1, the stamp: drops 8 lines a frame until the top row is at Y $76, then shakes the screen for 24 frames ($BEEE) with the crash sound $A5 and rises (state 2)
sets row 0's Y and the three below it, 21 lines apart
state 2: rises 8 lines a frame until the top row is above Y $3C, then moves sideways again (state 0)

state 3: flashes, black and white on alternate frames, for 30 frames ($BEF0). Then gives the screen back: no sprites of its own ($03ED), the multiplexer's interrupt and the scroll decision put back from $0872 and $0876, slots 9 and 10 emptied; slots 0 to 8 become debris (type 13), with the sounds $89 and $8A, and 10,000 points ($0211 = 1)
tests the screen under the boss for the hero's shots: the two outer columns over 8 character rows from the top row's Y, the three middle ones over 3 character rows from the third row's Y

tests one column: its X, halved with the high bit from $7287, less 12 and divided by 4, gives the screen column, and the Y in $6F45 the screen row (through $BF6E and $BF87); then it looks down X character rows for a character from $D8 up, one of the hero's shots
the operand of the LDA: the Y of the row the column's test starts at, written by boss_hits

a hit: a grenade ($DD) is told it has hit something ($1B) and a laser ($E0) is stopped ($017F); the shot's character is overwritten with $D4, the boss flashes ($BEED), and the weapon's damage from $0720 comes off its energy; below zero it is destroyed (state 3, 30 frames), otherwise the hit sound $98
hurts the hero when he is inside a box set by the boss's left column and top row, unless he is shielded ($BFFD) or the wheel ($2D)

the level's frame routine while it runs its own sprites ($0862): sets sprites 3 to 7 to the row in $0224, their pointers on both screens, X, high bits and colour (0 black, or 1 white while it flashes). If that row starts above the top of the play area it waits for the raster to come within 15 lines of the next row and moves the sprites down to it

the raster interrupt that replaces the multiplexer's while the boss is on ($071E): sets sprites 3 to 7 to the row in $0223 (pointers on the shown screen, X, high bits, colour); near the panel (raster line $CE or more) it hands over to the panel's interrupt. object type 3, the walking robot (sprites $98-$9B facing left, $9C-$9F right): walks along the ground, its four frames turning every sixth frame; turns round at a wall level with its body, hops up when its feet meet a step (the jump curve at $7453), and falls off ledges. Shot: an explosion and 100 points. Touching it hurts the hero, unless he is shielded or the wheel, which destroys it. The blast of a mine ($0305 negative; a grenade's blast is the engine's, $030D) knocks it off the screen in a death leap ($A0, $A1), also for 100. It keeps its frame delay, frame, direction and leap step in $BCF3, $BCFE, $BD09 and $BD14

The first shot opens it; then every fifth shot (the fourth the first time) throws out a prize for 500 points: a symbol picked at random from the first eight kinds (no 1UP or diamond), which leaps out, bounces off the screen's sides and lands as a bonus. After 15 prizes the next count blows it up for 5,000 points. Open, it is solid: the hero can stand on it, and jumping into it from below bumps it up
